There is a valid combinatorial mechanism behind this possibility. If a uniform permutation  $\Pi$  is genuinely independent of a selected physical fault set  $F$ , then for every virtual set  $A$ ,

 $\Pr[A\subseteq\Pi^{-1}F]
=
\frac{(|F|)_{|A|}}{(N)_{|A|}}
\le \rho^{|A|}
\qquad (|F|\le\rho N).
\tag{11}$ This is the desired support-spreading inequality. Its independence premise is essential. If the adversary knows the current permutation, it can choose  $F=\Pi(A)$ .

I did not construct a fixed-wire, bounded-arity routing implementation that maintains the required hidden-location invariant against persistent quantum probes while charging every routing layer and resource. Noiseless classical computation does not, by itself, provide that quantum routing operation.

Thus (11) is not a conversion of the user’s adversary into locally stochastic noise.
